resources.string: Read from the engine module itself, so a swapped or reflashed engine reports what it actually is.
Read what the modules say about themselves

All of this is service 0x1A, which only reads. The names come from the GDS2 catalogue, joined by identifier and by the length of the answer; the ones with no name are asked anyway, because what comes back is a measurement and a blank beside it beats a plausible guess.
Point an OBD app at this address and port. It runs as a foreground service, so the link survives a locked screen.
Reading live data. Keeping the link up with the screen off.
Connect the adapter and open a channel, then scan. Only parameters the vehicle reports as supported are listed.
Only what this car has (%1$d of %2$d)

The catalogue describes every configuration the marque ever shipped and cannot say which one this is — the GDS2 packages carry no model-to-variant table. Asking the module which identifiers it has takes a few minutes once and is remembered per vehicle.

Instead of asking for one parameter and waiting, the module is told to send a packet of them on its own — about a hundred times a second, against four or five a second between all of them by asking. Catalogue parameters from a single module only: a standard OBD PID is addressed to whoever answers, so it has no packet to belong to.
%1$d of the selection do not fit in the packets — seven of those hold forty-nine bytes between them — so those are polled instead. They still read, a few times a second rather than a hundred.
Pick a module. The catalogue covers every one the marque fits; the ones marked are the ones this car answered on, which needs a module sweep on the identification screen first.
A brand catalogue is every module configuration the marque ever shipped. Narrowing to one variant is what turns a list of thousands into a list you can read.
%1$d readable here, %2$d not: those carry an identifier or a width this tool has no request for — composite rows the factory tool builds a whole screen from, not parameters it is refusing you.
A pending code has been seen once but not often enough to light the lamp. OpenDash reads codes; it does not clear them.
Some monitors have not completed since the last reset
Press and hold on a chart to place a marker. It stays put while the recording scrolls under it, so the values follow along. Hold with two fingers to take it away.
Scanmatik was showing %1$d of these when the file was saved. All %2$d were recorded, and all %2$d are here.
Choose a folder outside app storage so recordings survive uninstalling the app.
Gzipped CSV. Over a 23-minute session: 3.63 MB plain, 0.60 MB compressed. Opens in a spreadsheet either way.
Requests are synchronous, so the adapter already sets the pace. Add a delay only to be gentle with a busy module.

Commanding a module moves parts on a vehicle that may have someone in or near it. The rows that name an output are always listed, with a padlock; this switch is what lets a command leave the app, and it closes again whenever the link drops.
This device has no screen lock, so actuation cannot be unlocked.
None installed. Standard OBD-II works without one.
Scoped to read one repository and revocable from the forge. Leave empty for a public repository.
For a host reached with an SSH key: a home server, a NAS, another machine. Files are fetched over SFTP.
Add the public key to the host as an authorised key, or to a forge as a deploy key. The private key stays on this device.

Joining from here pins the adapter socket to this network, so mobile data can stay on. The adapter calls itself DIRECT-SCANMATIK-#serial, so leaving the name blank and letting Android offer what is in range is the way to find it the first time.
Listing the networks in range needs permission. Tap Show networks to grant it, or leave the name blank and let the system picker do it.
Android returns no networks while location is switched off, whatever the app is allowed to do. Turn it on, or leave the name blank and let the system picker do it.
Nothing in range yet. The adapter takes a few seconds to raise its access point after it is plugged in. Join with the name left blank and Android offers its own list instead.
Android refused the scan: an app may only scan a few times a minute. Try again in a moment, or just join with the name left blank and pick from Android’s own list.
Choose a module first: a packet is declared in one module, so there is nothing to declare it in yet.

%1$d of the selection are standard OBD PIDs. Those are addressed to whoever answers rather than to one module, so they have no packet to belong to — untick them, or leave this off and everything is polled.
Bus filtered to four address ranges.
Bus unfiltered: the adapter is handing over every frame, which is slower and noisier. The narrowing step was refused.
Selections this catalogue publishes ready-made. Importing one puts it under Groups on the Live screen, against the module it belongs to.
No groups saved for this module yet.
%1$d of these rows name something the module drives rather than only measures. Unlock actuation in Settings to command them.

Actuation unlocked. %1$d rows name something this module drives. The identifier that reads a commanded output is not the one that sets it, and this module\'s control identifiers have never been observed, so only the release below is implemented.
The outputs this module drives, and its own status words for them: which request was refused, and why. The status rows carry no padlock because they are read like any other.
%1$d rounds of %2$d identifiers. Each parameter is live %3$.1f s in every %4$.1f s, at the full packet rate — instead of the ones past the tenth being polled a third of a time a second.

Five packets emit at about 96 Hz each and seven at about 51, so the module\'s fast configuration holds ten identifiers. With this on, a larger selection cycles through that configuration in rounds and everything gets the full rate part of the time. With it off, the first fourteen stream and the rest are polled a third of a time a second.
Switching rounds costs a stop and one declaration per packet — about a fifth of a second. Longer means less time lost switching and longer gaps for each parameter; shorter means the opposite.

A packet holds seven bytes of values, but the request that declares it only fitted two identifiers in one frame. Splitting that request across frames fits six — measured on this engine as three times the samples per second, at the same frame rate, with no extra traffic on the bus. It also halves the number of rounds, and a round change costs nearly two seconds. Turn it off if every round is refused and nothing ever emits.

What another car of this kind answered when it was asked, published by the catalogue. Taking one on lets this screen list what is worth recording with no car connected. It is a measurement of some other vehicle, not a fact about yours: ask this car when you have it.
Nothing to lay out yet. Choose some catalogue parameters of one module: a standard OBD PID is addressed to whoever answers, so it has no packet to belong to.
Each round emits for %1$s s and is then dark for %2$s s. A transient in that gap is not recorded at all.
Wider than a packet, so these are polled one at a time instead — far more slowly, and never at the same instant as anything else.

The order is not cosmetic. Two identifiers next to each other share a packet, a packet arrives in one CAN frame, and one frame is one instant. Two values you mean to compare must sit together; split across rounds they were never measured at the same time.
%1$d cells in %2$d rows. This file holds a saved screen, not a recording: there is no series in it to chart.
GitHub could not be reached. On the adapter\'s Wi-Fi there is no internet, so this is expected there.
Commands sent to the car\'s modules. The module lets go of every one of them by itself after about a minute, or at once with Release everything. Nothing here is for a moving car.
This catalogue lists no actuators. Update it from Settings, Catalogues.
No answer to the release. Switching the ignition off and on releases everything too.
Low risk — read the warning, then fingerprint
Affects the engine — checklist, 0 km/h before every command, screen lock
Changes stored values — all of the above, the name typed and 10 s to think
Do not touch — all of the above, a sentence typed, 30 s, and the screen lock again before every command
To enable it: open this output in GDS2 under Output Controls with the capture running, and add its CPID to actuators.tsv.

To see an output working, select what shows it in Live (for the EGR: air flow, engine speed, fuel), start the live view, then open this screen. The command panel charts those values.
The live view is stopped, so nothing is charted here. Start it in Live to watch the command land.
